_doc: RUNTIME LIGHT RIGS FOR TOWNS WHOSE cameras.json CARRIES NONE.
defaults.lightRig FIRST, because that is the file tools/cine_bake.py bakes the
plates from — one source, no copy, no drift. This file is the FALLBACK, and it
exists for exactly one town: Dellhollow's plates were baked with a full rig that
was never written into its cameras.json, so the bake reads nothing, applies
nothing, and the blend's own lights are what land in the picture.
EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS A MEASUREMENT WITH ITS INSTRUMENT NAMED. Nothing here was
chosen. If a town later gains a real defaults.lightRig, delete its block here —
a fallback that shadows a live source is the drift this project keeps paying for.
dellhollow.cameras.json should carry defaults.lightRig with exactly the numbers
below. Written with today's values it is a NO-OP for the bake (cine_bake would
set the objects to what they already are) and it retires this file. It was not
done in this lane because dellhollow.cameras.json belongs to the Dellhollow lane.

_derivation: INSTRUMENT 1 — the blend, read directly. tools/blends/dellhollow-master.blend
copied to scratch (the lane was mid-write on the original) and opened headless:
204 lights, of which exactly ONE is a SUN.
SUN_key   energy 12.0   color (1.0, 0.79, 0.56)
World Background  color (0.8, 0.8, 0.8)  strength 2.1
View  AgX / 'AgX - Medium High Contrast' / exposure 0.15
Through play3d's own sunDirFromBlender (the transform the overworld lane
verified against cast shadows) that is direction-to-sun (0.741, 0.598, -0.305),
ELEVATION 36.7 deg — a real daylight key, not the skylight-only frame that
del-cine/cine.json's `"sunEnergy": null` suggests. That null means only that
cameras.json named no sun for the bake to override; it is not a statement
about the blend.
INSTRUMENT 2 — the rig, already written down. tools/look_golden.py IS this
light: 'SUN_key energy 5.0 -> 12.0, color -> (1.0, 0.79, 0.56),
rotation_euler.x -> 0.93 (Y and Z are the district builds azimuth and are NOT
touched), World strength 1.6 -> 2.1'. 0.93 rad = 53.28 deg, which is the blend's
53.285 to three decimals. The two instruments agree.
CORRECTION TO look_golden.py's OWN DOCSTRING, recorded here because it will
mislead the next reader: it glosses rotation_euler.x 0.93 as '~53 deg
elevation'. 53.3 is the rotation, and the ELEVATION is 90 - 53.3 = 36.7 deg.
The repo's verified conversion is unambiguous (Emberbrook's (56,0,212) is
recorded at elevation 34 in play3d's overworld block), so the docstring is
off by the complement.
THE AZIMUTH WAS CROSS-CHECKED BEFORE THE BLEND WAS OPENED, and this is the
part worth keeping. tools/gate_light.py's header states 'SUN_key's direction
is -0.86,-0.35,-0.38'. Inverting that through the same transform gives
rot_x 67.9, rot_z 111.8 — the rot_z matches the blend's 112.38 to half a
degree, and the rot_x does NOT, because that comment predates look_golden.py
moving the sun from 1.1858 rad to 0.93. A stale note that is right about the
half nobody changed.
